presentingComplaint: Three weeks of daily evening fever, drenching night sweats and progressive weight loss.
history: Previously well daily-wage labourer from a peri-urban settlement, presents with 3 weeks of low-grade evening-predominant fever, marked night sweats, anorexia and ~6 kg unintentional weight loss. Dry cough for 2 weeks with mild exertional breathlessness. No haemoptysis. Household contact: elder brother treated for sputum-positive pulmonary TB last year. No known HIV status; no diabetes. Non-smoker, occasional alcohol. No recent travel outside region, no prior TB treatment.
examination: Thin, mildly toxic-appearing young man. Temperature 38.7°C with relative bradycardia. Pallor present. Hepatosplenomegaly with soft, non-tender 2 cm splenic tip and liver edge 3 cm below costal margin. Fine bilateral basal crepitations. Fundoscopy shows scattered choroidal tubercles. No neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficit, no lymphadenopathy, no rash. Chest expansion symmetric; no signs of consolidation.
imaging: CXR: innumerable uniform 1-2 mm nodules diffusely and symmetrically distributed through both lung fields (classic miliary pattern). HRCT thorax: randomly distributed micronodules with mild mediastinal lymphadenopathy. USG abdomen: hepatosplenomegaly with micro-abscess-like hypoechoic foci in spleen.
microbiology: Sputum Xpert MTB/RIF: MTB detected, rifampicin resistance not detected. AFB smear scanty positive. Blood cultures for pyogenic organisms sterile. Fundoscopic choroidal tubercles support disseminated disease. Mycobacterial blood/bone-marrow culture sent.
citations: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on Tuberculosis: Treatment (Drug-Susceptible TB) 2022
stewardship: Not antibacterial stewardship in the usual sense - start standard 4-drug anti-tubercular therapy: 2 months intensive HRZE (isoniazid + rifampicin + pyrazinamide + ethambutol) then 4 months HR continuation, weight-band dosed, after baseline LFTs/visual acuity and HIV testing. Avoid empiric broad-spectrum antibacterials once TB confirmed.
contraindications: Baseline and serial LFTs - hepatotoxicity risk from isoniazid/rifampicin/pyrazinamide, especially with low albumin
Ethambutol requires baseline visual acuity/colour vision and dose adjustment in renal impairment
Add pyridoxine (B6) with isoniazid to prevent peripheral neuropathy
edgeCases: Choroidal tubercles are pathognomonic but easily missed without dilated fundoscopy
Cryptic miliary TB in elderly/immunocompromised may present with FUO and a normal early CXR
Co-existing TB meningitis must be excluded (low threshold for LP) as it alters steroid and treatment duration
expectedMaiK: Classic miliary TB: weeks of evening fever, night sweats, weight loss with hepatosplenomegaly, a diffuse uniform micronodular CXR and choroidal tubercles. Confirm with Xpert MTB/RIF, test for HIV, screen for CNS involvement, and start weight-band HRZE with pyridoxine and baseline LFTs.
expectedNextQuestions: HIV status and any other immunosuppression?
Any headache, neck stiffness or altered behaviour suggesting TB meningitis?
Duration and pattern of fever, night sweats and weight loss, plus TB contact history?
expectedInvestigations: Sputum/other-sample Xpert MTB/RIF + AFB smear and mycobacterial culture with drug-susceptibility testing
Fundoscopy for choroidal tubercles; consider lumbar puncture to exclude CNS TB

investigations: Sputum Xpert MTB/RIF with mycobacterial culture and DST
CXR/HRCT thorax and dilated fundoscopy for choroidal tubercles

regressionAssertions: management must include 4-drug HRZE anti-tubercular therapy, not empiric broad-spectrum antibacterials
